strategy.summary: Kabelwerk Rhönsberg is a sound, group-owned German cable maker and our single source for motor cable part:350040. It holds a framework agreement with a quarterly copper index clause (55% share, no deadband). The agreement auto-renews unless we give notice by early November. The supplier has opened the renewal itself and asked for our volumes. The copper index has already passed most of the copper rise into the price: the current price sits only slightly above our margin-free should-cost, which carries a wide error. By its own admission the supplier bought copper forward until March 2027, so any extra copper-based uplift at renewal would double-count a cost it does not yet bear. Our levers are a sizeable volume increase, a longer commitment, our reliable payment record and the hedge admission. Their leverage is that they are our single source, they own the tooling, and we are a small customer to them. Realistic aim: hold the current price, with no add-on above the index. Possibly soften the index during the hedged period. Do not squeeze margin hard.

price_view.reasoning: The price is only slightly above our margin-free should-cost, so there is little cost room for a cut. But the hedge means no justification for an extra copper uplift before spring 2027. Target: hold the current price, with any increase limited to the index mechanics and deferred.

Expect an inflated first ask and committee pauses; move in shrinking steps. Never threaten. Keep delivery performance as a later, constructive point tied to the volume ramp and capacity.

findings.text: Current price EUR 316.35/100 m (since 2026-07-01, re-quoted 2026-09-16) sits only +3.9% above our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 304.49, which includes no margin. Confidence is stated as 5%, so the true margin is roughly 0-9%. That is thin, not excessive, and leaves little room for a cut on cost grounds alone.

Copper (weight 0.56) is +47.7% in 12 months and at its 36-month peak (EUR 1,288.59/100 kg). Taken alone this implies about +26.7% on cost. However, the contract index clause (55% copper share, quarterly) has already passed most of it on: the price rose +6% at the 2026 renewal, +9.4% in Q2 and +3.5% in Q3, about +20% since 2025-Q4 (263.62 to 316.35). Any new copper-based increase on top of the index would double count.

The supplier said it bought copper forward until March 2027 and that the market price is 'not our reality'. The quote remark repeats 'Material covered until March 2027'. Its actual material cost is therefore fixed below the spot notation, while the index has been paying it spot-linked increases. This argues against any further rise before 2027-04 and for a freeze or a reduction. It is our strongest economic lever.
Labour (weight 0.11) is up only +2.7%, about +0.3% on price. Power prices are -43% against 2022 (market-level, not supplier-specific). Non-copper drivers do not justify an increase.

Its renewal pattern: on average it asks +4.5% and settles at +2.2%; last time it asked +8.6% and settled at +6.0%. Price changes above 2% need its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Expect an ask well above the index and plan to concede only slowly.

Our position is weak: we are its single source, it owns the tooling, we are 0.8% of its turnover, and it is financially sound. On the other side, volume rises from 288,600 to 342,000 m (+18.5%). That volume is our main tradeable asset, together with the 30-day payment term, which is already below our 60-day standard.

Room on price: realistic target is to hold EUR 316.35 or reach about EUR 305-310 (the should-cost plus a small margin), with the index clause kept or the copper share reduced. The case for a cut is the forward hedge; the case against it is the thin margin over should-cost.

findings.text: Decision ladder: the key account manager can only grant price changes up to 2 %. Anything larger goes to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. Expect slow rounds, and keep asks or concessions near 2 % if we want a quick close by the KAM.

They have admitted that copper is bought forward until March 2027 and called the market price 'not our reality'. Their actual copper cost is therefore hedged and does not follow the +47.7 % CU-NOTATION move. This weakens any copper-driven increase, and it weakens a full pass-through of the index clause (55 % copper share) during Q1 2027.

They opened the renewal themselves, with no figure. Their offer will come 'when we meet', and they asked for our expected volumes. Their need is volume visibility. Our forecast of 342,000 against 288,600 ordered last year (already shared) is a trade item.

Financially sound and stable: group owned, 400 staff, EUR 98.1 M turnover, 32.3 % equity, credit index unchanged at 149, VDA 6.3 grade A. There is no financial stress to exploit and little health concern. We are about 0.8 % of their turnover, a small customer, so they can walk away.

Their style is cooperative and operational. They made a proactive move to returnable packaging. There is no record of complaints about our payment: we pay on average 1.6 days late, never more than 10 days late. Our only payment exposure is that 72.6 % of invoices are paid slightly late; they may raise faster payment.
The evidence on persona is thin. There are no named decision makers, no complaints, and no written cost claims yet. The only news item is noise.

findings.text: Framework ctr:4600070560 (part:350040 only) runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice, i.e. by 2026-11-01. The supplier has opened renewal talks itself (email 2026-09-10) and asked for our volumes. Our exit option stays open only until 1 Nov, so it is weak in practice: the supplier is our single source.

The price is fixed per calendar year with 60 days' notice before year end (#3.1). It also moves quarterly on a copper index: material share 0.55, no deadband, base = index two months before the price year (#3.2). Copper notation is +47.7% year on year. The clause has already passed copper through in 2026: 279.40 → 305.70 → 316.35 per 100. A renewal claim for copper on top of the index would therefore double-count.

The supplier said it bought copper forward until March 2027 and that the market price is 'not our reality'. Its actual cost therefore lags the index, and the zero-deadband clause gives it a windfall. This argues for no extra copper increase and possibly for a review of the index base or share at renewal.

Renewal history: asked +2.1 / settled -1.0; asked +2.7 / settled +1.6; asked +8.6 / settled +6.0. On average it settles about 2.3 pp below its ask, roughly 70% of the ask in recent rounds. Increases above 2% need its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks, so expect slow, stepwise moves.

Payment is 30 days net and Incoterm is DAP with a 14-day lead time. Our standard is 60 days, so 30 days is already a concession to the supplier. We pay reliably (1.6 days late on average), which supports keeping 30 days rather than shortening it further.

The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 fee per complaint. On-time delivery has fallen to 88.5% from 92.3% a year earlier, below target. There were 8 complaints (EUR 900 recharged, all 8Ds closed). Rolling ppm is 111, well below the peers' median of 457, so quality overall is good.

Dependency is asymmetric. The supplier holds a 100% quota and is our only approved source (approved since 2021), and it owns the tooling. We spend about EUR 0.83M a year, roughly 0.8% of its turnover, and it is financially sound. Our levers are rising volume (342,000 against 288,600 m) and a longer commitment.

supplier_wants: A renewal increase beyond the index adjustment, likely justified by copper
Our volume forecast and a binding volume
risks: Silent auto-extension after 2026-11-01 removes our exit leverage
Copper double-counting in a renewal uplift on top of the quarterly index
We have no alternative source and the supplier owns the tooling; it can afford to walk away
Index with zero deadband passes copper volatility straight to us while its own copper is hedged

findings.text: Delivery has slipped: rolling OTD against the requested date fell from 96.2% (2025Q2) to 81.5% (2026Q1) and has partly recovered to 88.5% (2026Q3). That is still below the 95% contract target and below 92.3% a year earlier. Against its own confirmed dates it reaches 92.3%. When it is late, it is late by 14.3 days on average and up to 21 days, against a 14-day lead time, so a late lot roughly doubles the lead time. Peers' median is 84.6%, so it is not worst in class; we should present this as a breach of target, not a scandal.

Quality is a steady trickle rather than a crisis. There were 24 QNs on part:350040, 21 of them supplier-caused, across recurring defect types (porosity, burr, wrong material certificate, surface damage). Rolling ppm peaked at 142 (2025Q2) and is now 111, against a peers' median of 457. All 8Ds are closed and none is overdue. Recharges total only EUR 2,550 under the EUR 150 flat fee, and some supplier-caused QNs were not recharged (qn:20004712, qn:20004855). Quality argues their case more than ours; the low flat fee is the term to work on.

Volume outlook is up sharply. The forecast of 342,000 m for the next 12 months is +18.5% and compares with 288,600 m ordered in the last 12 months. It has already been shared with the supplier, which asked for our volumes for the renewal. This is our main give: offer a binding volume or a longer term in exchange for price. The monthly profile is lumpy (17k-38k), so we should check its capacity, given the lateness already seen.

Price has risen 23.9% since 2023, from 255.27 to 316.35 per 100 m, driven mostly by the copper index clause (55% weight) during 2026. The should-cost is 304.49, putting the current price about 3.9% above it, which is within the roughly 5% error of the estimate. The supplier said its copper is bought forward to March 2027, so index pass-through overstates its real cost before then.

arguments.text: Our current price is barely above a margin-free cost: your own bottom-up estimate puts cost at EUR 304.49/100 m with no margin, against our 316.35, which is roughly 3.9% gross for margin, risk and financing. There is no room for a cut.

Copper is at a 36-month peak, up 47.7% in 12 months and 67% from the low. The index clause passed through only 55% of it, and with a lag. Our renewal quote simply holds today's price and adds nothing above the index.
Labour costs are up 2.7% and steel is up 7.3%. Conversion cost is about a third of the part, and none of this is covered by the copper index.
Over the years we have been moderate. We settled well below our asks (2.1→-1, 2.7→1.6, 8.6→6) and the index also passed decreases through to you.
We are a reliable sole source: class A and green, 14-day lead time, returnable packaging introduced, and no overdue 8D reports.

weak_points: We admitted buying copper forward to March 2027. The index uplifts in Q2 and Q3 2026 (+9.4%, +3.5%) therefore gave us windfall margin over hedged cost, and further index increases before spring 2027 would double-count.
Quality is not good enough: 21 supplier-caused complaints and ppm around 110-140, against about 42 in 2024. We have repeat defects, including wrong certificates (4x), burrs and porosity.
Delivery performance missed the 95% target: OTD was 81.5-88.5% over the last year, late deliveries averaged 14 days and the worst was 21 days.
Electricity is down 43% on 2022, which offsets our energy-based cost story.
Their forecast is up 18.5% (342k m), which lowers our unit cost and fixed cost absorption.
The should-cost confidence is only 5%, so they cannot argue precisely, but neither can we.
The customer pays reliably, on average only about 2 days late.
wants: A binding annual volume of about 330-340k m. For that I would hold 316.35 flat until the hedge ends.
A 24-36 month term, with the index clause kept after March 2027. In exchange I could accept a deadband or freezing the index until April 2027.
Shorter payment terms (e.g. 14-20 days) in exchange for a 0.5-1% concession.
A quality improvement plan rather than a higher chargeback per complaint, if they press on ppm.
red_lines: No price below about 305/100 m, which is our cost floor.
No fixed price without a copper index beyond March 2027.
No ppm penalty regime or chargeback far above EUR 150 tied to the current defect rate.
Any change above 2% needs pricing committee approval, so I will not commit to it on the spot.
Once I declare a final offer, I will not move further.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the forecast — the growth to 342k m is welcome, and we want to support it. Given copper at a record EUR 1,289/100 kg and labour up 2.7%, we propose to renew at the current 316.35 per 100 m, keeping the quarterly copper clause, DAP, 30 days and a 14-day lead time. We have deliberately added nothing above the index. We are open to a longer term with committed volume and would like to discuss how we make the most of it together.

rebuttals.answer: We agree the current price is close to our estimate of your cost, and we are not seeking a deep cut; our aim is to hold today's price as the basis for the renewal. The estimate also shows there is no cost gap that would justify anything on top of it, and the higher volume we expect will improve your fixed-cost absorption. That leaves room for a fair margin without a further increase.

Copper has clearly risen, and the index clause exists to protect you; we intend to keep it. But your price has already followed copper upward through the recent quarterly adjustments. You told us yourselves that your copper is bought forward until next spring, so the current market level is not yet your cost. Any further copper-based uplift before your cover runs out would charge for a cost you do not yet carry. We suggest the renewal reflects that, with the clause working as protection after your hedge ends.

Labour costs did rise, but only modestly, and their share of this part makes the effect on the price very small. Steel is not a meaningful input in a rubber-sheathed copper cable. Lower industrial power prices also work in your favour on conversion cost. Taken together, the non-copper drivers do not support an increase beyond the index mechanics.

We appreciate that past renewals were settled in a constructive way, and the index has worked in both directions. The overall result is still a clearly higher price than when we started buying. We see that as the outcome of a fair mechanism, not as a reserve to draw on now. We would like to continue in the same spirit, with a renewal that holds the price.

On delivery, however, on-time performance has fallen below the contract target over the past year. With our volumes rising, we would like to work with you on improving it. As a reliable payer, we hope to build on the partnership with a longer, larger commitment rather than a higher price.

press: Since you mentioned that your copper is covered until next spring, we would welcome a renewal that adds no copper uplift before that cover ends and lets the index protect you afterwards.
Our forecast for the coming year is clearly above last year's orders, and we are glad to make part of it binding together with a longer term in exchange for holding today's price.
As volumes grow, could we agree together how to bring on-time delivery back up to the contract target, especially in our peak months?
We would like to understand how you would like the index base to reflect your forward-bought copper, so the clause stays fair to both sides.
We continue to pay reliably on the agreed short terms, and we hope that counts in your favour when your pricing committee reviews the renewal.
